spec.join: _panelsplit_arm_cells harvests panel/summary/each era/each year; count columns and bp-year columns are joined together and split apart again in answers, because an event count moving and an event's cost moving are different findings
spec.control: the same arm joined against itself; every cell must read delta 0.0 or the join machinery moved the numbers

cutoff_control.comparison: old raw arm vs today raw arm (arm held fixed)

answers.delta_units: counts are event/name counts; total_book_bp and bp_per_year are basis points, years is a duration -- the summary max is a screen over mixed units, not a quantity

irreducible_core.note: what is left after the repair is not 'clean': it is resumptions, non-integer prints and instruments whose daily limit is not 10/20%, which the screen never claimed to fix

answers.reading: the split census is an arm statement: 40 of 73 cells move (26 count, 14 value) and 0 cell(s) exist on one arm only
answers.honest_flag: event-count cells are EXPECTED to move: the repair targets exactly the prints this leg counts, so a count delta is the repair working, not instability

honest: descriptive census only: no gate, no verdict on the strategy, no prereg, no trial count, no ledger booking
the repair edits the panel this leg censuses, so counts moving is the expected outcome and is not evidence about any other face
the screened arm keeps every name (neutralise_int repairs the print, it does not drop the symbol), so names/breadth cannot move -- that is a property of the mode, not proof the panel is clean
the screen flags arithmetic impossibilities rather than confirmed corporate actions; the residual core still contains ETFs, resumptions and non-integer prints, so 'repaired' never means 'clean'

E97 counts the published numbers of this runner; the join covers the panel/summary/era/year cells, not the ranked top-event list or the screening pointers (the headline event identity is compared separately as a date face)
